title: When the Vector Turns
premise: Astrid Ishikawa, navigator of the colony ship Meridian, has spent thirty years tending a navigation beacon that no one else knows exists—a lie he inherited from the dead captain whose backups sleep in the hold. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream of a turning vector, Astrid realizes the beacon is broadcasting, and something on the other side of the jump window is answering. The lie he must keep alive—that Meridian is alone in the dark—is all that prevents two hostile fleets from converging on the fragile colony. In the end, Astrid wakes the captain's backups, merges his own memories with hers, and broadcasts the truth: the beacon was never a warning, but an invitation, and the children's shared dream is the second fleet's way of asking to become family.
about_author: Noor Nakamura is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about the signals we send and the ones we pretend not to hear. She lives in a coastal town where she keeps a lighthouse log as a writing ritual and insists she is not superstitious, only attentive.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet him maintaining the hidden beacon during night shift, haunted by the cryo-bay backups and the captain's dying instruction to keep it secret. A child named Sef catches him at the antenna array and mentions a dream about a turning line of light. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by the first intrusion of the outside world.

chapters.title: Shared Frequencies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Astrid and twelve-year-old Sef. The dream spreads through the colony's children; council elders grow suspicious of Astrid's unexplained power draws. He decodes fragments of the beacon's return signal and finds the captain's voice inside it—she lied to him too. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as inheritance; grief becoming curiosity.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Window
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, escalating to climax. The jump window opens early; a scout fleet detects the beacon and a second, older fleet answers from deep space. To keep them apart, Astrid must sustain the lie that Meridian is armed and alone—but the children, dreaming in unison, override the beacon with their own signal. Emotional beat: terror yielding to surrender, as Astrid realizes control was always an illusion.

chapters.title: What the Vector Turns Toward
chapters.summary: Astrid and Sef share POV in resolution. Astrid wakes the captain's backups and lets her memories braid with his, finally understanding the beacon was an invitation, not a shield. The two fleets answer the children's dream not with weapons but with coordinates for arrival. Emotional beat: found family completed across generations, species, and fleets—the invisible man made visible at last.
